## Reading this

- **This is the rig FR-004's diagnosis rests on.** It attributes nothing by itself -- `reports/009-diagnosis/`'s cause-attribution work reads this table's deltas and assigns each to a denominator, normalization, or vocabulary cause.
- A name absent from one arm (`csv`-only or `html`-only) is not a parsing difference; it is an enumeration difference between the two acquisitions and is reported separately, never folded into a class delta.
- **The `html`-mode residual measured here (79/2422, 3.3%) disagrees with the carried figure
  (206/2422, 8.5%, `reports/option-taxonomy/2026-08-15.md`).** Both are stated rather than one
  overwriting the other. The corpus is live and `008` landed multiple grammar productions
  (`_COMPLETION_VERBS`/`_COMPLETION_HEADS`) between that date and this run, which is the expected
  direction and magnitude of the move -- not a measurement defect. FR-009 criterion 1 (options
  parity) must therefore be read against **this** run's html baseline once T030 lands, not against
  the pre-008 figure.
- **`csv` class 11 ("footnote fragment", an extractor-bug class in `html` mode) carries 288 of the
  437 `csv`-mode unparsed rows (65.9%) here, far above the ~30-row / 5.3%-of-residual figure
  `plan.md` finding 8 sizes for the two extraction-artefact shapes together.** This table does not
  attribute causes -- that is Phase 3's job -- but the size of the delta is recorded here because it
  bears directly on FR-006's hypothesis (a): a `csv`-mode row whose markup survives `strip_field`'s
  anchored `_TAG` pattern (`plan.md` finding 6) can present as a short fragment carrying no
  recognised verb, which is exactly class 11's rule. Whether that is the actual mechanism, or a
  genuine denominator population this classifier's html-tuned rule order simply was not built to
  separate from real footnote fragments, is unresolved by this run and is explicitly Phase 3's
  attribution work (T036-T044), not Setup's.

## Same-name collision set, six Space Marine factions, `csv` mode (T002)

Measured directly against a live `Datasheets.csv` acquisition and the already-published
`data/wh40k-11e/factions/f-{black-templars,blood-angels,dark-angels,deathwatch,space-marines,
space-wolves}/datasheets/` trees (roster names only; no MFM fetch needed, since the roster is
points-enumerated and unaffected by this migration, C1) -- discarded after this run, counts only.

**This measures a different question than `docs/follow-ups.md` item 4's html-mode 53**, and the
difference is itself the finding. Under `html` mode each chapter has its own page, so a name shared
across chapters (e.g. a generic Terminator Squad) produces one row **per page** -- a cross-page
enumeration collision the chapter-keyword rung was built to narrow. Under `csv` mode the export
does not model chapters at all (`Factions.csv` has 25 rows, no per-chapter entries): a
chapter-shared unit is **one row**, `faction_id=SM`, not six. That is not an export-side ambiguity;
it is exactly what the faction-scoped `unit-map.json` stage-1 entry (T022-T024, plan.md finding 4)
is for -- one curated pairing, adopted once per faction scope.

The question this measurement actually answers: within the export's own `faction_id=SM` rows, how
many **display names carry more than one distinct `datasheet_id`** -- a genuine export-side
ambiguity no faction-scoping can resolve, because both candidates already live in the same faction.

| | Count |
|---|---:|
| `Datasheets.csv` rows with `faction_id=SM` | 292 |
| Distinct names among them | 282 |
| Names with >1 distinct `datasheet_id` | 10 |
| ...of which, the name also appears in the published six-chapter roster | 10 |
| Published roster, distinct names across all six chapters | 281 |

Refined by Legends status (`curate/assemble.py::_legends_source_ids`'s own `source_id` resolution,
reused rather than re-derived -- structural, no source name printed):

| Collision shape | Count |
|---|---:|
| Both candidate rows current (non-Legends) -- a genuine disambiguation need | 9 |
| One Legends + one current -- resolvable by the existing Legends-marker rung alone | 1 |
| Both Legends | 0 |

**Sizes Open Decision O2 tighter than the carried 53 figure**: the export-side collision set FR-016
must actually demonstrate a resolving rung for is **9**, not 53 -- the other ~44 of the html-measured
53 are ordinary per-chapter roster duplication that the faction-scoped stage-1 fix (T022-T024)
already resolves by construction, never reaching `match.py`'s disambiguation rungs at all. Whether a
publication-id, detachment-linkage, or curated-crosswalk rung resolves those 9 is Phase 5's
measurement (T067, research.md Q3), not Setup's.

## Digest churn, ability summaries, `csv` mode (T004)

`tools/churn_dry_run.py --` no code change, run as it exists -- against a live `csv`-mode
acquisition. Non-destructive; nothing under `curation/` written; the acquired text discarded with
`work/` at run end. Report: `reports/churn-dry-run/2026-08-18.md`.

| Authored | Approved | Would need re-review | Share of approved | Absent from source |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2125 | 2125 | **76** | 3.6% | 97 |

**Disagrees sharply with the spec's carried framing** that the ~2,125-record ability volume is
"unavoidable" churn because export-sourced text will not byte-match html-scraped text "even where
the mechanic is identical" (spec US3). Measured, under the CURRENT (pre-T030) normalization, only
**3.6%** of approved ability summaries would actually need re-review -- not the near-total wave the
spec's prose implies. This is consistent with `ip_strip.py`'s normalization being strong enough
that most mechanics reduce to identical canonical text regardless of which arm's markup wrapped
them, and is exactly the kind of measurement FR-002 requires taken before Open Decision O3 is
decided, rather than assumed from the byte-identity argument alone.

**Scope note**: this run, like the tool itself, covers `curation/abilities/` only. It does **not**
measure the spec's other cited classes -- 324 approved detachment-rule records, 28 faction-rule
records, 70 glossary entries -- because `tools/churn_dry_run.py` has no code path for them today.
Extending it, if Phase 6 needs a churn figure for those classes before US3 begins, is not a Setup
task and is not done here.
